title: Mini project: to-do list logic
summary: Combine closures, arrays and objects to build a small to-do list module with add, toggle, remove and filter.

quiz.explain: `filter` keeps the items for which the function returns true. Two todos have `done` equal to false.

quiz.q: Which line flips the `done` value of a task object named `t`?
quiz.explain: `!` turns true into false and false into true. Assigning the result back toggles the value.

quiz.q: Remove the task with the given id by keeping all the others.
quiz.explain: `filter` builds a new array without the unwanted item. That is the usual way to delete from an array by value.

quiz.q: Why does the module return `items.slice()` (a copy) from `list()` instead of `items` itself?
options: So outside code cannot change the hidden array by accident
JavaScript does not allow returning arrays
quiz.explain: If you returned the real array, any caller could push or delete things behind your back. Returning a copy keeps the data private, one of the benefits of closures.

exercise.task:
In `todo.js`, finish `createTodoList()`. It returns an object with these functions, all sharing a hidden array of todos:

- `add(text)` trims the text. If it is empty, it returns `null` and adds nothing. Otherwise it adds `{ id, text, done: false }` and returns that todo. Ids are 1, 2, 3, ... in order and are never reused, even after a removal.
- `toggle(id)` flips `done` of the matching todo and returns `true`. If the id does not exist it returns `false`.
- `remove(id)` deletes the matching todo and returns `true`, or `false` if it does not exist.
- `list(filter)` returns a new array. `'all'` (the default) gives every todo, `'active'` only those not done, `'done'` only those done.
- `remaining()` returns how many todos are not done.
hints: Keep `let items = [];` and `let nextId = 1;` inside `createTodoList`, and return an object whose functions use them. That is a closure.
Use `items.find((t) => t.id === id)` to locate a todo. `remove` can compare the array length before and after `filter`. `list` can use `filter` for the two cases and `slice()` for all.
